title: Q&A: Why a pivotal IPCC meeting in Ethiopia ended in ‘profound disappointment’ - Carbon Brief
gist: IPCC-65 in Addis Ababa ended suspended with no AR7 timeline (sixth failure running) and no budget, as India, Saudi Arabia, Russia and allies blocked a schedule delivering the impacts and mitigation reports before the 2028 global stocktake and held budget lines hostage. The IPCC faces a funding crisis — US contributions stopped after 2024 and the trust fund could be depleted by end-2028 — while nearly 120 authors pledge to keep working.

insights.claim: For the sixth consecutive time, countries at the IPCC's 65th session in Addis Ababa failed to agree a publication timeline for the seventh assessment report (AR7), and chair Jim Skea suspended the talks on Friday evening with no decision.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: The IPCC's ability to deliver consensus science on schedule is now structurally impaired, not a one-off failure.
insights.quote: Countries have failed – for the sixth time running – to agree on the timeline
insights.locator: Countries have failed – for the sixth time

insights.claim: IPCC-65 was effectively the last plenary at which a stocktake-aligned timeline could be agreed, because Skea had said publishing all reports by end-2028 required a decision before the end of 2026.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Absent a resumed session in late 2026, the WG2/WG3 reports likely miss the second global stocktake at COP33.
insights.quote: In April, Skea told Carbon Brief that publishing reports by the end of 2028 would only be possible if a decision was taken before the end of 2026.

insights.claim: The three pre-meeting options all approve WG1 in May 2028 but diverge on impacts and mitigation: the co-chairs' Sofia plan approves WG2/WG3 in June/July 2028, the Lima revision in July/Sept 2028, and the India/Saudi Arabia submission pushes WG2 to April 2029 and WG3 to July 2029.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: The fight is specifically over whether adaptation and mitigation science (the policy-relevant reports) lands before or after the stocktake.

insights.claim: During the week the number of timeline options ballooned to seven before shrinking to four, including a Haiti proposal approving WG1 in April 2028, WG2 in July 2028 and WG3 in October 2028.

insights.so_what: Option proliferation signals negotiation used as delay rather than convergence.

insights.so_what: Procedural endurance favours blocking parties in consensus bodies.

themes.theme: Bloc politics: delay coalition vs stocktake coalition

insights.claim: India, Kenya, Russia and Saudi Arabia are the loudest voices for publishing the impacts and mitigation assessments after the 2028 stocktake, arguing developing countries need more time to prepare, review and approve reports; Iran, Iraq and China also backed a looser link.

insights.so_what: A petrostate-plus-large-emerging-economy bloc can now veto the scientific input to the Paris ratchet.

insights.claim: Both camps weaponise 'inclusivity': delay advocates cite developing-country capacity, while small-island states argue delay most harms the climate-vulnerable, with Vanuatu invoking the ICJ's 2025 advisory opinion on binding climate obligations.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Equity framing is being used on both sides, so it no longer resolves disputes in UN climate fora.

themes.theme: IPCC funding crisis and US withdrawal

insights.claim: IPCC contributions in 2025 were 5.3m Swiss francs lower than in 2023 while costs rose, and by early July 2026 only 16 countries and organisations had contributed a total of 2.8m Swiss francs.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Voluntary-funded science bodies are visibly starved; 2026 run-rate is well below the minimum need.

insights.claim: The secretariat says AR7 needs about 33m Swiss francs to complete (just over 8m per year), with a bare minimum of 5.8m per year, and warns that at 2025 contribution levels the trust fund would be depleted by end-2028, preventing delivery of AR7.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Funding, not just politics, could independently kill on-time AR7 delivery.
